summary: Iter11 — Round 2 features (file delete, outcome predictor, cost estimator, hearing transcriber, legal aid, case share links, stats wall). Backend pytest: 13/13 PASS after I fixed a critical bug in /api/hearing/transcribe (wrong kwarg name on OpenAISpeechToText + BSON-unserialisable response object). All 5 new dashboard tiles, Stats Wall, Outcome modal end-to-end (95% ring + Strategy + Working For You + Risks all rendered), Cases→case-detail→share-case-btn all verified live on mobile viewport 390x844 against the public URL.

minor.issue: FIXED in this iteration. The implementation was calling OpenAISpeechToText.transcribe(file_path=...) — the actual library signature is transcribe(file=...) and the return value is a TranscriptionResponse object (not a string). Both bugs would have made the entire Hearing Recorder feature error 500 on any upload. I changed server.py to (a) pass file=open(tmp,'rb'), and (b) extract .text/.get('text') before persisting to Mongo (otherwise the BSON encoder throws InvalidDocument). Suggest the main agent code-review this fix and consider adding a unit test that mocks OpenAISpeechToText.

design_issues.screen: Outcome / Cost / Hearing / Legal Aid modals on mobile (390x844)
issues: Modal content is taller than the viewport so the primary CTA (e.g. outcome-run-btn, hearing-upload-btn) sits below the fold; the user must scroll inside the modal. Works, but a sticky-footer CTA pattern (the way the Letter Reader modal already does it) would feel more polished and prevents 'where is the button?' confusion on smaller phones.

action_items: [VERIFY] Main agent: review the hearing-transcribe fix in /app/backend/server.py around L3019-3033 — confirm the file-handle pattern + .text extraction is acceptable (the temp file is unlinked after close).
[OPTIONAL] Make Outcome/Cost/Hearing/Legal-Aid modals match the Letter Reader pattern (sticky footer CTA) so the primary button is always visible on small phones.
[OPTIONAL] On the Outcome modal, render the recommended_strategy AFTER 'working for you' / 'risks' (currently it's above) — feels more natural to read pros/cons → plan.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:3019 (pre-fix) — used OpenAISpeechToText.transcribe(file_path=...) — wrong kwarg. The lib signature is transcribe(file=...). Resulting 500 swallowed by the broad try/except as 'Transcription failed: …'. **High-priority test gap** — no unit test exercised this endpoint until this iteration. Fixed.

server.py:3020-3023 (pre-fix) — the return value of stt.transcribe() is a TranscriptionResponse pydantic-ish object, NOT a string. It was being stored directly into Mongo as the 'transcript' field, which BSON cannot encode → InvalidDocument. Fixed by extracting .text. Same issue would re-surface anywhere else this lib is used; recommend a small helper `_stt_text(resp)` and re-using it.
server.py:3014 — the 50MB upload guard happens AFTER reading the entire body into memory. Consider streaming or rejecting on Content-Length first.
server.py:3082 — legal-aid means test hardcodes the £2657/£8000 thresholds. These change annually; pull from a config or env so it can be updated without a deploy.

server.py:3164-3185 — /stats/public cache is per-process via Mongo doc; works, but the in-memory variant comment is misleading. Either implement true in-process caching with a TTL dict or remove the comment.

Outcome/Cost endpoints fall back to {success_probability_pct: 0, …} when the LLM JSON parse fails — this could look like the user's case has 0% chance of success rather than a parse error. Consider returning a 502 + 'try again' instead.

rca of the issue: BUG (hearing/transcribe 500) — RCA: emergentintegrations.llm.openai.speech_to_text.OpenAISpeechToText.transcribe() takes `file` (not file_path) and returns a `TranscriptionResponse` object whose `.text` attribute holds the transcript. server.py:3019-3020 passed file_path=… → TypeError surfaced as 'OpenAISpeechToText.transcribe() got an unexpected keyword argument file_path'. Reproduction: POST /api/hearing/transcribe with any audio multipart → 500. Fix applied (server.py L3019-3033): open(tmp.name,'rb') as fh, pass file=fh, then transcript = resp.text if hasattr(resp,'text') else (str(resp) or ''). Verified: TestHearingTranscribe + TestFileDelete (which uses hearing to create a file) all pass.
